featured_reviews.review_text:
The doctor and staff were kind, but I'm sharing this so others can set appropriate expectations or ask detailed questions beforehand.
I paid ₹4,500 for a carbon facial with pico laser, but the experience was far below expectations for this price point.

Key Issues:
After the treatment, I was moved to another room to apply a mask, then asked to wash it off myself at a sink. Some more patients were sitting around waiting in masks—it felt more like a crowded waiting area than a proper treatment space.

No extractions included: This means if you went in with a few acne and comedones, you'll be going back with them. I had to specifically request whitehead removal, and they agreed to do it only on my nose.

Poor communication: Before each step, I had to ask what they were doing as nothing was explained. Responses were vague—"it's nothing, just RF" or "just some mist." When I asked about the mask they were applying, I was told "it will make you feel cold"—not what it actually does or what it is.

Billing confusion: I confirmed on the phone that the ₹4,500 included consultation to discuss which facial suits my needs. After treatment, they tried charging an additional ₹1,000. When I reminded them of our conversation, they denied it. Thankfully, the doctor intervened and waived the fee.

The doctor mentioned several times that she was including extra steps since it was my birthday. While I appreciate the thought, it felt awkward and made me wonder what the standard ₹4,500 treatment actually includes, as the basics seemed quite limited.

I chose this clinic based on its location in Hiranandani, assuming a premium area would mean premium service, but the experience felt more like a budget salon than an upscale dermatology clinic.
